slot.brief: Probability of at least one of several independent events using complement counting; e.g., system reliability or 'at least one'.

stem: A system has three parallel paths, each with two components in series. The component success probabilities on the paths are $(\dfrac12,\dfrac23)$, $(\dfrac34,\dfrac45)$ and $(\dfrac13,\dfrac12)$, respectively. All six components work independently. Find the probability that the system works.

verdicts.working: Series-path success probabilities are 1/3, 3/5, and 1/6. Thus the system failure probability is (2/3)(2/5)(5/6)=2/9, so its success probability is 1−2/9=7/9.

working:
$P(A_1)=\dfrac13,\quad P(A_2)=\dfrac35,\quad P(A_3)=\dfrac16$
$P(A_1\cup A_2\cup A_3)=1-\prod_{i=1}^3(1-P(A_i))$
$=1-\left(\dfrac23\right)\left(\dfrac25\right)\left(\dfrac56\right)=\dfrac79$

Independent check: Series-path success probabilities are 1/3, 3/5, and 1/6. Thus the system failure probability is (2/3)(2/5)(5/6)=2/9, so its success probability is 1−2/9=7/9.
solution:
For each series path, multiply the component success probabilities: $P_1=\frac13$, $P_2=\frac35$, and $P_3=\frac16$. The parallel system fails only if all three paths fail:
$$P(\text{works})=1-\left(1-\frac13\right)\left(1-\frac35\right)\left(1-\frac16\right)=1-\frac29=\frac79.$$
